title: Performance Briefcase: Compact Route & Model Board (prototype & chart specs)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a compact, scannable dashboard panel ('Performance Briefcase') that surfaces correlated per-model and per-route signals for latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, token flow, and cost-per-token in a single compact canvas. The briefcase is intended for product engineers and platform owners who need a fast triage surface that fits into the Console route list and can be opened as an overlay without leaving context. This ticket covers visual design, micro-interactions, chart specs, and a high-fidelity prototype for usability testing.

Scope and features: 1) Top-row summary chips: rolling p50/p95 latency, success rate, rps, token/sec, cost/hr. 2) Token-burst heatmap (compact) aligned to routes to show where bursts concentrate across time windows. 3) Ridgeline latency percentiles per model variant allowing quick comparison across variants. 4) Cost-per-token sparkline with on-hover breakdown by token type (input/output). 5) Inline microtrace peek: small tappable timeline that expands into a lightweight microtrace modal. 6) Time-range scrubber with pin/compare mode (compare last-1h vs prev). 7) Keyboard-accessible focus mode for screen-reader and high-contrast palettes.

Chart/interaction specs included: quantile ridgeline should render up to 6 variants, use stacked translucent fills with edge outlines for p50/p95, with consistent color mapping per model. Token-burst heatmap uses log-scaled buckets to keep dynamic range readable. All charts support hover tooltips, keyboard focus, and a compact legend that toggles series visibility. Prototype includes animated transitions for switching time ranges and toggling variants to preserve context.

Design constraints and non-goals: This component must be lightweight — not intended to replace the full Route Performance Console. We'll exclude deep query/filter builder and long-term retention UIs from this ticket. Aggregation granularity will be 1m for <=24h and 5m for >24h.

Accessibility and theming: Ensure WCAG AA contrast in default theme; provide a high-contrast theme token. All interactive elements must be tab-navigable. Provide aria-labels for sparklines and ridgelines and ensure screen reader-friendly summaries for the top-row chips.

Artifacts: Figma prototype, PRD link, GH branch for data contract and a short Loom walkthrough are attached below.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype linked and validated in 2 rounds of moderated usability tests (N=6 engineers)
Chart spec document with axis/scale/bucket rules and color tokens delivered
Design handoff tokens and component variants published to the Console design system
Accessibility checklist verified and signed off by Accessibility reviewer
Engineering alignment on two data contracts (heatmap aggregates and percentile snapshot) and a demo integration PR merged into feature branch
decisions: Use log-scaled buckets for token-burst heatmap to compress bursty distributions
Keep default displayed variants to 3 with 'show all' option to avoid visual noise
Render ridgeline percentiles client-side with precomputed percentile snapshots from backend to avoid streaming overhead
Compact layout will prioritize vertical density over expanded legends; detailed legend appears in expanded panel
tradeoffs: Precompute percentiles reduces backend CPU but increases storage for snapshots (chosen for lower tail latency)
Client-side ridgeline rendering adds browser CPU load for many variants; we limit to 6 concurrently visible variants
Using log scale improves readability for spikes but may hide subtle shifts in low-volume routes; we include linear toggle in tooltip
review_feedback: PM Mateo Rivera: prefer default time-range to be 1h to show live behavior; agreed and set preference with quick toggle
Eng lead Priya Nair: backend will expose percentile snapshots on a 30s cadence; design updated to show last-calc timestamp in the chip
Accessibility reviewer Liam O'Connor: requested larger focus rings and explicit aria summaries for sparklines; implemented in notes
Security reviewer Elena Kovács: confirmed no PII in the briefcase surface; approved
